stands.notes: Desktop series: two tiers of adjustable height and rake on a powder-coated aluminium frame. Jaspers name their stands by tier count and inner width in centimetres, and it is the inner width that decides whether a synth fits between the uprights. The 2DT ships with four 30 cm holders, so a tier carries two instruments unless you buy more. Tier heights and angles are set by whoever builds it, so the ones in a project are the placement's, not the maker's.
Desktop series, 120 cm between the uprights. See the 2DT-105B for how the range is named and what the tier figures mean.
Desktop series, the widest of the three at 149 cm inside. See the 2DT-105B for how the range is named.

Floor-standing two-tier, 110 cm to the top of the uprights. Depth and tier depth are taken from the same generation of frame as the 3R; Jaspers do not publish a per-tier depth, so treat that figure as the shelf run rather than a quoted specification.
Three tiers on castors. The R series rolls, which is worth knowing on a plan: it can be pulled out to get behind it.
Four tiers, 120 cm inside, 140 cm to the top of the uprights. The common studio size.
Six tiers, 170 cm to the top. Tall enough that the upper tiers are above eye level, which is what the rake on them is for; check the top shelf against your ceiling and against anything it will block.
